question: 18-year-old boy with breast pain and retroareolar nodule on palpation. What is the most frequent cause?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Pubertal gynecomastia -> hormonal changes during puberty -> breast tissue growth in males -> 80% CHAIN: Pubertal gynecomastia -> common in adolescent boys -> benign condition -> 75% CHAIN: Pubertal gynecomastia -> typically resolves on its own -> self-limiting condition -> 80%
enhanced_information: Pubertal gynecomastia is the most frequent cause of breast pain and retroareolar nodule in an 18-year-old boy. This condition is common in adolescent boys, typically benign, and often resolves on its own. The evidence paths support the hormonal changes during puberty leading to breast tissue growth in males, which aligns with the consensus understanding of pubertal gynecomastia.
